title: Sunday · lockboxes in rain
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: October: the summer over, the tourists gone, the lockboxes still on every door, rain running off them. Twelve gray boxes on twelve doors on an empty street.

panels.composition: Tier 1: main street in October rain, empty, the row of old houses, a gray lockbox on each door with rain running off it.

image.prompt: a small-town street of old wooden houses in October rain with a gray key lockbox on every front door and no one anywhere, no words

panels.name: Street

panels.composition: Tier 2: one box, close, rain beading on its dial. Nobody has turned it since August.

image.prompt: close on a gray key lockbox on a door with rain beading on its dial, no words

panels.name: Box

panels.composition: Tier 3: four doors down: her porch, the box on the knob, the step wet, the light off. Held.

image.prompt: an old wooden house's porch in rain with a lockbox on the doorknob and the porch light off, no words

panels.name: Porch

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: The boxes after the season. Her porch, dark.
